#: The proof is the slow part (15 to 25 minutes). This job reuses one
exactly as bootstrap.yml and `just app` do: the cache key only finds a
candidate, and `xtask
proof-reuse` accepts it only if its attestation binds this checkout,
this image's Lean and Lake, the architecture and every input file. A
tag or a manual run proves in full. A reused proof leaves no holo, so
the holo is then built (six minutes, no proof) and must carry the very
build ID the reused attestation verified, or this job fails.

steps.name: The proof of these exact proof inputs, kept by an earlier page build

with.key: prism-page-proof-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-sdk-${{ steps.proof-inputs.outputs.sdk }}-lean-${{ steps.proof-inputs.outputs.lean }}-${{ hashFiles('app/**', '!app/specs/**', 'prismpm.lock', 'Justfile', 'rust-toolchain.toml') }}

#: This job keeps its own proofs: bootstrap.yml proves inside `just vv`,
and a holo built here never carries the build ID of a proof made
there (seen on main: same inputs, different build). A page proof is
reused only by a later page build, under the same read-time check.
app/specs is not a proof input: the proof reads the lexlean project
(app/src, app/language and app's own files), and a spec reaches it only
through the .lex.tex a generator writes into app/src. So a change to the
specs alone reuses the proof (xtask proof.rs INPUT_PATHS says the same).

steps.name: On main, the proof the merged pull request's page build kept
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
head=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$SHA/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null)][0].head.sha // empty')
test -n "$head"
run=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/pages.yml/runs?head_sha=$head&event=pull_request&status=success&per_page=1" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty')
test -n "$run"
gh run download "$run" --repo "$REPO" --name prism-page-proof --dir .prism-proof
echo "candidate proof from the merged pull request's run $run"

#: A cache a pull request saves is never visible to main, so main proved
every merge again (16 to 22 minutes). The merged pull request's own page
build keeps its proof as an artifact; main takes it as a candidate only.
`xtask proof-reuse` still accepts it only if it binds main's checkout,
and any failure here just means: prove in full.

steps.name: Build and verify the holo through the locked SDK
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
image=$(sed -n 's/.*"sdk_image":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' prismpm.lock)
if [[ ! $image =~ ^[a-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?/[a-z0-9./_-]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]; then
  printf '%s\n' 'prismpm.lock does not select an immutable SDK image' >&2
  exit 64
fi
docker_config=$(mktemp -d)
# The SDK's /tmp is a private directory on the runner's own disk, as
# bootstrap.yml has it since template 1cb0d36: the patched SDK's build
# outgrows a fixed 2 GiB tmpfs.
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$scratch/prismpm-home/.docker"
trap 'rm -rf "$docker_config" "$scratch"' EXIT
printf '{}\n' >"$docker_config/config.json"
docker run --rm \
  --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
  --group-add "$(stat -c '%g' /var/run/docker.sock)" \
  --volume "$scratch:/tmp" \
  --volume "$PWD:$PWD" \
  --volume /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  --volume "$docker_config:/tmp/prismpm-home/.docker:ro" \
  --workdir "$PWD" \
  --env DOCKER_CONFIG=/tmp/prismpm-home/.docker \
  --env BUILDX_CONFIG=/tmp/prismpm-buildx \
  --env HOME=/tmp/prismpm-home \
  --env PRISMPM_EPHEMERAL_HOME=1 \
  --env PRISM_PROOF_EVENT \
  --env SDK_IMAGE="$image" \
  "$image" bash -c '
    set -euo pipefail
    # The one way a holo is built when a proof is reused.
    # PrismPM 0.4.0 refuses a provenance statement here: the lock
    # sits at the root, not beside the app. `verify` writes the
    # same holo without one (a487fb6a for #94 both ways), and the
    # build-id check below is what binds it to the reused proof.
    build_holo() { prismpm --project "$1" build --no-provenance; }
    # A pull request proves in full, so main'"'"'s reused-proof build
    # never runs on it. Rehearse that build alongside the proof, on
    # a copy of this tree, so a change that breaks it fails here
    # and not in main'"'"'s deploy (#94 blocked main this way).
    rehearsal=
    if [[ ${PRISM_PROOF_EVENT:-} == pull_request:* ]]; then
      mkdir -p /tmp/rehearsal
      tar --exclude=./.git --exclude=./app/.prism --exclude=./.prism-proof --exclude=./target -cf - . | tar -xf - -C /tmp/rehearsal
      (cd /tmp/rehearsal && build_holo app) >/tmp/rehearsal.log 2>&1 &
      rehearsal=$!
    fi
    just app
    if [[ -n $rehearsal ]]; then
      if wait "$rehearsal"; then
        echo "main'"'"'s reused-proof build works on this tree: $(tail -n 1 /tmp/rehearsal.log)"
      else
        cat /tmp/rehearsal.log >&2
        printf "%s\n" "main'"'"'s reused-proof build fails on this tree, so merging it would block the deploy" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
    fi
    shopt -s nullglob
    holos=(app/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
    if [[ ${#holos[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
      proved=$(grep -o "\"build_id\": *\"[0-9a-f]\{64\}\"" .prism-proof/verified/manifest.json | grep -o "[0-9a-f]\{64\}")
      test -n "$proved"
      build_holo app
      holos=(app/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
      test ${#holos[@]} -eq 1
      built=$(basename "$(dirname "${holos[0]}")")
      if [[ $built != "$proved" ]]; then
        # Not the build the reused proof verified: that proof says
        # nothing about this holo, so prove this tree in full.
        printf "the holo built here (%s) is not the build the reused proof verified (%s): proving in full\n" "$built" "$proved" >&2
        rm -rf app/.prism .prism-proof
        PRISM_PROOF_EVENT= just app
        holos=(app/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
        test ${#holos[@]} -eq 1
      else
        echo "the holo is build $built, the build the reused proof verified"
      fi
    fi
  '

guests: A decision change is a spec change: a pull request whose decision guests
are older than their modules gets them rebuilt here, in the locked SDK the
proof uses, as the artifact `stale-guests` laid out at its repository
paths. `gh run download <run> -n stale-guests` and a commit bring them in,
so no one needs the SDK image locally. GU-01 (tools/guests/gen.py check)
still fails until they are committed.

name: Publishes the repository's app page: `site/` with the holo that `just app`
builds and verifies through the locked SDK. Project content, not universal
policy: a repository may extend or replace it.
It runs on every push to main, beside `bootstrap`, not after it: `just app`
is the proof-bearing build (the Lean kernel checks every theorem before the
holo exists), so the page goes live as soon as that passes, while the rest of
the gate runs on both architectures. The SDK step and the signing step are
the ones `build.yml` runs, copied here: the gate pins every `uses:` to a
commit and so forbids calling a workflow by path. When `build.yml` changes
either step, copy it again. The page then carries the same holo that
`prism-code build --remote github` would hand a device, with the signed
provenance of the run that made it beside it.
concurrency: A newer push to a pull request cancels its older run. Main's gates run as
soon as each merge lands, beside each other (a queued merge waited 12 to 27
minutes for the one before it); only the publish job is one at a time, never
cancelled, and it publishes only main's head, so an older run that finishes
later never puts an older page back.

steps.name: Collect the holo, its build directory and what this run knows about them
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
shopt -s nullglob
holos=("$PROJECT"/.prism/build/*/*.holo)
if [[ ${#holos[@]} -ne 1 ]]; then
  printf 'expected one holo, found %d\n' "${#holos[@]}" >&2

build_id=$(basename "$build_dir")

out="$RUNNER_TEMP/prism-build"

fingerprint=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8")).archive_fingerprint)' "$build_dir/application/holo-identities.json")

' "$out" "$(jq -cn \
  --arg repository "$REPOSITORY" --arg sha "$SHA" --arg run_id "$RUN_ID" --arg run_url "$RUN_URL" \

  --arg project "$PROJECT" --arg build "$build_id" --arg holo "$name" --arg fingerprint "$fingerprint" --arg sha256 "$sha256" \

{

  echo "holo=$name"
  echo "fingerprint=$fingerprint"
  echo "path=$out"
  echo "holo-path=$out/build/$name"

name: Builds and verifies the repository's app on a GitHub runner, and hands the
holo back as a signed artifact, so no machine of the author's needs Docker,
the SDK image or a toolchain. Project content, not universal policy: a
repository may extend or replace it.
Three ways in, one job:
- `prism-code build --remote github` pushes one commit to a ref under
prism/build/ and waits for this run; the run's head SHA is that commit
and nothing else, whatever the author's branch does meanwhile.
- `pages.yml` calls it on every push to main, then publishes the page from
the artifact it leaves. The SDK step lives here and nowhere else in the
project's workflows; `bootstrap.yml`, universal policy, keeps its own.
- Run workflow, from the Actions tab or GitHub Mobile.
What the artifact `prism-build-<sha>` holds: the holo, the build directory
beside it (`manifest.json`, `application/`), `build.json` naming the commit,
the repository, the run and the holo's fingerprint, and
`provenance.sigstore.json`, this run's signed provenance from
actions/attest-build-provenance. The signer is this repository's workflow
through GitHub's OIDC issuer, and the statement's subject is the holo's
SHA-256, so a holo from another commit, another repository or another
workflow is refused by whoever checks the bundle. The device that downloads
the artifact verifies the holo again itself: the build is not trusted, it
is checked.

steps.name: Compare main's head with what is deployed, and act
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
label=deploy-blocked
title='The live page is behind main: its deploy is blocked'
head=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/main" --jq .sha)
committed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$head" --jq .commit.committer.date)
age=$(( $(date +%s) - $(date -d "$committed" +%s) ))
run=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/pages.yml/runs?branch=main&head_sha=$head&per_page=20" \
  --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.event == "push" or .event == "workflow_dispatch")] | sort_by(.created_at) | last // empty')
issue=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues?state=open&labels=$label&per_page=1" --jq '.[0].number // empty')
say() { printf '%s\n' "$*" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"; }

if [[ -z $run ]]; then
  # A push from a workflow token starts no workflow; give the push
  # trigger five minutes, then start the deploy and the gate here.
  if (( age < 300 )); then
    say "main is at $head, committed ${age}s ago; its deploy has not started yet"
    exit 0
  fi
  say "main is at $head and nothing deployed it: starting pages and bootstrap on main"
  gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/pages.yml/dispatches" -f ref=main
  if [[ -z $(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/bootstrap.yml/runs?branch=main&head_sha=$head&per_page=1" --jq '.workflow_runs[0].id // empty') ]]; then
    gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/bootstrap.yml/dispatches" -f ref=main
  fi
  exit 0
fi

id=$(jq -r .id <<<"$run")
status=$(jq -r .status <<<"$run")
conclusion=$(jq -r '.conclusion // ""' <<<"$run")
attempt=$(jq -r .run_attempt <<<"$run")
url=$(jq -r .html_url <<<"$run")

if [[ $status != completed ]]; then
  say "main is at $head; its deploy is $status: $url"
  exit 0
fi

if [[ $conclusion == success ]]; then
  say "main is live at $head: $url"
  # Every pull request merged since the last live page is told, once, on
  # its own page that it is live: the publish job opened the published
  # page in a fresh Chromium (PG-01, PD-01, PD-02 live), so nobody
  # checks by hand.
  # Main's runs go side by side and only the head's publishes, so the
  # last few runs before this one may not have published: tell from the
  # oldest of them (already-told PRs are skipped below).
  before=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/pages.yml/runs?branch=main&status=success&per_page=6" \
    --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.head_sha != \"$head\") | .head_sha] | last // empty" 2>/dev/null || true)
  commits=$head
  if [[ -n $before ]]; then
    commits="$before $(gh api "repos/$REPO/compare/$before...$head" --jq '[.commits[].sha] | join(" ")' 2>/dev/null || echo "$head")"
  fi
  done_prs=" "
  for commit in $commits; do
    for pr in $(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$commit/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null) | .number] | join(" ")' 2>/dev/null || true); do
      [[ $done_prs == *" $pr "* ]] && continue
      done_prs+="$pr "
      seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$pr/comments?per_page=100" --jq '[.[] | select(.body | startswith("Live:"))] | length')
      [[ $seen == 0 ]] || continue
      gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues/$pr/comments" -f body="$(printf '%s\n' \
        "Live: this change is on the published page, as main \`$head\`." \
        "" \
        "The publish job opened the published page in a fresh Chromium and its live checks passed (PG-01, PD-01, PD-02): $url")" >/dev/null
      say "told #$pr it is live"
    done
  done
  if [[ -n $issue ]]; then
    gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues/$issue/comments" -f body="Live again at $head: $url" >/dev/null
    gh api -X PATCH "repos/$REPO/issues/$issue" -f state=closed -f state_reason=completed >/dev/null
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Which job and step refused, in the run's own words.
failed=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$id/attempts/$attempt/jobs" \
  --jq '[.jobs[] | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled" or .conclusion == "timed_out")] | first // empty')
job=$(jq -r '.name // "unknown job"' <<<"${failed:-{\}}")
step=$(jq -r '[.steps[]? | select(.conclusion == "failure" or .conclusion == "cancelled")] | first | .name // "unknown step"' <<<"${failed:-{\}}")
job_url=$(jq -r ".html_url // \"$url\"" <<<"${failed:-{\}}")

if [[ $job == 'publish the page' && $attempt -lt 2 ]]; then
  say "main's publish failed at \"$step\" on attempt $attempt; running the failed jobs once more: $url"
  gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$id/rerun-failed-jobs"
  exit 0
fi

# The checks that refused, by name, from the job's own log.
job_id=$(jq -r '.id // empty' <<<"${failed:-{\}}")
tests=""
if [[ -n $job_id ]]; then
  tests=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/jobs/$job_id/logs" 2>/dev/null \
    | sed -nE 's/^[0-9TZ:.-]+ +not ok [0-9]+ - (.*)$/- \1/p' | sort -u | head -n 10 || true)
fi
# The pull requests whose merge made main's head: the thread that merged
# one hears about it on its own pull request, not only in the issue.
prs=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$head/pulls" --jq '[.[] | select(.merged_at != null) | .number] | join(" ")' 2>/dev/null || true)

live=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/pages.yml/runs?branch=main&status=success&per_page=1" \
  --jq '.workflow_runs[0] | "\(.head_sha) (\(.updated_at))"' 2>/dev/null || echo unknown)
body=$(printf '%s\n' \
  "main's deploy is blocked, so the live page is not main." \
  "" \
  "| | |" \
  "| --- | --- |" \
  "| main | \`$head\` |" \
  "| refused by | **$job** / **$step** |" \
  "| run | $job_url |" \
  "| live page is | \`$live\` |" \
  "| merged by | ${prs:+#${prs// / #}} |" \
  "" \
  "${tests:+Checks that refused:}" \
  "${tests}" \
  "" \
  "Every gate that refused here also runs on pull requests, so the fix lands as a pull request; this issue closes itself when main is live again.")
say "$body"
gh label create "$label" --repo "$REPO" --color d93f0b --description 'The live page is behind main' --force >/dev/null
if [[ -n $issue ]]; then
  last=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$issue/comments?per_page=100" --jq 'last | .body // ""')
  [[ $last == "$body" ]] || gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues/$issue/comments" -f body="$body" >/dev/null
else
  gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues" -f title="$title" -f body="$body" -f "labels[]=$label" -f "assignees[]=$OWNER" >/dev/null
fi
# Once per pull request and commit: the PR whose merge was refused is told
# on its own page. The same merge result already passed there, so a refusal
# now means a check that does not decide the same way twice.
for pr in $prs; do
  seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$pr/comments?per_page=100" --jq "[.[] | select(.body | contains(\"$head\"))] | length")
  [[ $seen == 0 ]] || continue
  gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues/$pr/comments" -f body="$(printf '%s\n' \
    "Merging this pull request made main \`$head\`, and main's deploy refused it, so the live page is not this change." \
    "" \
    "Refused by **$job** / **$step**: $job_url" \
    "${tests:+}" \
    "${tests}" \
    "" \
    "These are the same gates this pull request passed. If its checks ran on the same merge result, the refusal comes from a check that does not decide the same way every run: make that check deterministic in a new pull request.")" >/dev/null
done

name: Keeps the live page on main's newest commit, or says loudly that it is not.
After every pages run, every 20 minutes, and on demand, it looks at main's
head and the page's runs for it:
- no deploy was ever started for it (a merge that triggered nothing):
start one;
- the publish step failed on its first attempt (Pages or the live check
can be transient): run the failed jobs once more;
- a gate refused it: open, or update, one issue that names the commit, the
failing step and the run, assigned to the owner, so the stall is seen;
- it is live: close that issue.
It never re-runs a gate that refused, and never deploys anything but main.

if: Repositories made from this template have no Pages site for this page.

steps.name: Check out main
Test each ready pull request on main and the train before it
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
git config user.name "merge train"
git config user.email "merge-train@train.invalid"
main=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
echo "main=$main" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
image=$(sed -n 's/.*"sdk_image":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' prismpm.lock)
[[ $image =~ ^[a-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]{1,5})?/[a-z0-9./_-]+@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$ ]]
scratch=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT
fast_gates() {
  python3 -I tools/realize/gate.py --check &&
    python3 -I tools/standards/gate.py --check --base "$main" &&
    python3 -I tools/parts/gate.py &&
    python3 -I tools/product/gate.py &&
    python3 -I tools/guests/gen.py check &&
    { [[ ! -f tools/handwritten/gate.py ]] || python3 -I tools/handwritten/gate.py; } &&
    docker run --rm \
      --user "$(id -u):$(id -g)" \
      --volume "$scratch:/tmp" \
      --volume "$PWD:$PWD" \
      --workdir "$PWD" \
      --env HOME=/tmp/prismpm-home \
      --env PRISMPM_EPHEMERAL_HOME=1 \
      --env SDK_IMAGE="$image" \
      "$image" bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; mkdir -p "$HOME"; just fmt-check model template-check lint test'
}
ready=()
while read -r number head draft fork; do
  [[ $draft == false && $fork == false ]] || continue
  ok=true
  for name in "page / gates" "acceptance / ubuntu-24.04"; do
    state=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/$head/check-runs" -f check_name="$name" -X GET --jq '[.check_runs[] | .conclusion][0] // "pending"')
    [[ $state == success ]] || ok=false
  done
  if $ok; then ready+=("$number:$head"); fi
done < <(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls?state=open&base=main&sort=created&direction=asc&per_page=50" \
  --jq '.[] | "\(.number) \(.head.sha) \(.draft) \(.head.repo.full_name != .base.repo.full_name)"')
echo "ready: ${ready[*]:-none}"
accepted=()
: >"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
for entry in "${ready[@]}"; do
  number=${entry%%:*}
  head=${entry#*:}
  before=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
  git fetch -q origin "$head"
  if ! git merge -q --no-ff --no-edit "$head" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    git merge --abort || true
    printf '%s %s %s\n' "$number" "$head" "it conflicts with main ($main) and the pull requests the train takes before it" >>"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
    continue
  fi
  # The pull request's own code runs without the token.
  if (unset GH_TOKEN; fast_gates) >"$RUNNER_TEMP/gates-$number.log" 2>&1; then
    accepted+=("$number:$head")
    echo "#$number $head: the fast gates pass on main and the train before it"
  else
    tail -n 40 "$RUNNER_TEMP/gates-$number.log"
    printf '%s %s %s\n' "$number" "$head" "the fast gates refuse it merged with main ($main) and the pull requests the train takes before it; see run $GITHUB_RUN_ID" >>"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
    git reset -q --hard "$before"
  fi
done
echo "accepted=${accepted[*]:-}" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
# The refusals travel to the merge job as an output: a run cannot download its
# own artifacts while it is still running.
cat "$RUNNER_TEMP/refused"
echo "refused=$(base64 -w0 <"$RUNNER_TEMP/refused")" >>"$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#: Ready: open, from this repository, not a draft, and both required
checks passed on its head. The fast gates are the ones that take
seconds to minutes: the page job's model gates natively, then the
workspace's format, model, template, lint and test gates in the
locked SDK. The proof is not repeated: main's own run binds it.

steps.name: Switch GitHub's auto-merge off, merge the accepted in order, and say why the rest wait
steps.run:
set -euo pipefail
query='mutation($pr: ID!) { disablePullRequestAutoMerge(input: {pullRequestId: $pr}) { clientMutationId } }'
gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=50" --jq '.[] | select(.auto_merge != null) | .node_id' |
  while read -r id; do gh api graphql -f query="$query" -f pr="$id" >/dev/null || true; done
# Every open pull request learns once, from the pipeline, how it merges.
notice="Merge train notice"
gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls?state=open&base=main&per_page=50" --jq '.[].number' |
  while read -r number; do
    seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$number/comments?per_page=100" | jq --arg m "$notice" '[.[] | select(.body | startswith($m))] | length')
    if [[ $seen == 0 ]]; then
      gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues/$number/comments" -f body="$(printf '%s\n' "$notice: the merge train merges this pull request once it is green on current main; don't enable auto-merge." '' '---' '_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_')" >/dev/null || true
    fi
  done
expected=$MAIN
for entry in $ACCEPTED; do
  number=${entry%%:*}
  head=${entry#*:}
  now=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/commits/main" --jq .sha)
  if [[ $now != "$expected" ]]; then
    echo "::notice::main moved to $now outside the train; the next run tests #$number again"
    break
  fi
  if ! expected=$(gh api -X PUT "repos/$REPO/pulls/$number/merge" -f sha="$head" -f merge_method=merge --jq .sha); then
    printf '%s %s %s\n' "$number" "$head" "GitHub refused the merge (see run $RUN)" >>refused-merge.txt
    break
  fi
  echo "merged #$number at $expected"
done
mkdir -p refused
printf '%s' "$REFUSED" | base64 -d >refused/refused.txt
cat refused-merge.txt >>refused/refused.txt 2>/dev/null || true
while read -r number head why; do
  [[ -n $number ]] || continue
  marker="Merge train: $head"
  seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/issues/$number/comments?per_page=100" | jq --arg m "$marker" '[.[] | select(.body | startswith($m))] | length')
  if [[ $seen == 0 ]]; then
    gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/issues/$number/comments" -f body="$(printf '%s\n' "$marker: not merged, because $why. Fix it on this branch (merge main first) and the train tests it again." '' '---' '_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_')" >/dev/null
  fi
done <refused/refused.txt

#: GitHub's own auto-merge would merge behind the train's back.

name: Two pull requests that each pass their gates against an older main can
still break main together: #105 and #110 were each green, and together
ST-01 refused main. So nothing merges on its own. The train merges a pull
request only after the fast gates passed on it merged with main as main is
now, together with every pull request the train takes before it.
One run at a time. The test job has a read-only token and runs each ready
pull request's code. The merge job never runs that code: it merges the
accepted pull requests in order, and only while main is still where they
were tested.
